subject: Private deployment follow-up: VPC/on‑prem networking & residency recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Arun Mohan <arun.mohan@northbridgehealth.com>, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: private deployment requirements & next steps

Hi Arun / Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call so we have alignment and clear next steps. TL;DR: you need a Private deployment (VPC or on‑prem) driven by regulatory/data residency constraints and an air‑gapped environment for certain workloads.

Key pain points / goals we captured:
- Air‑gap requirement for PHI ingestion pipeline on a dedicated on‑prem floor (no outbound internet from that subnet).
- Data residency: all model input/output for patient records must stay within North American infrastructure (preference: us‑east‑1 or on‑prem).
- Networking constraints: strict egress controls, limited open ports, internal CA only; certificate provisioning likely offline.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + HIPAA audit evidence required; long retention of audit logs (3+ years).
- Timeline: pilot that integrates with your ETL within Q2, production by Q4 pending approvals.

What Redwood can do (summary):
- Private (VPC) deployment for cloud + dedicated Private control plane option for restricted workloads.
- On‑prem packaged option that can be installed behind your firewall / air‑gapped environment.
- Support for customer KMS/HSM, offline certs, and configurable egress rules; we can run in a network segment without outbound internet and exchange artifacts via signed bundles.
- We will provide a network port list, certificate expectations, and a sample network diagram for your security team.

Proposed immediate next steps (we agreed on):
1) I’ll send a short network requirements spreadsheet and a one‑page architecture diagram for your IT/security to review (attached).
2) Vivek to schedule a technical session with your IT/infra team to map firewall rules and cert flow.
3) You’ll share the completed security questionnaire and an initial list of stakeholders (IT, Security, Legal, Compliance).
4) We’ll propose an initial PoC scope and SOW for a small air‑gapped pilot.

Attachments: redwood_private_overview.pdf, network_requirements.xlsx

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll correct. Otherwise I’ll coordinate the SE call for next week.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Date: 2026-03-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: private deployment requirements & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks accurate and very helpful. Couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Air‑gapped environment: yes, the floor is fully segmented. We can provide an internal CA for certs; no public‑CA issuance permitted for that network.
- Egress: only outbound to a designated proxy is allowed, controlled by our IT team; ideally we’d avoid any external callbacks.
- Data residency: for regulated patient data we must never leave our on‑prem SAN. We may start with a VPC deployment for non‑PHI workloads.
- Audit logs: our compliance team requires signed, tamper‑evident logs with 3 years retention — is that something Redwood can provide?

I attached our initial security questionnaire (security_questionnaire_filled.pdf). Please review the bits around key/material handling and telemetry. Also, can you confirm which ports/protocols Redwood needs open for the on‑prem package to talk to your support/control plane (if any)? We prefer an offline install but will discuss a design for periodic artifact exchange via secure USB or SFTP into an air‑gapped gateway.

Sofia — looping you for scheduling the infra session with IT Ops.

Regards,
Arun Mohan
VP Engineering, Northbridge Health
arun.mohan@northbridgehealth.com

Subject: Re: Recap: private deployment requirements & next steps

Arun — great questions. Short answers inline below, and a couple of attachments that should help your security and network teams.

- Internal CA / certs: we support customer‑provided certs and can ingest your internal CA chain during an offline install. No public CA required.
- Egress: an offline/on‑prem installation is fully supported. If you choose the Private control plane option, we typically need an outbound channel for telemetry and billing; however, we can route through a customer‑controlled proxy or opt for batched, signed telemetry uploads via SFTP or USB transfer for air‑gapped segments.
- Ports/protocols: minimal ports required for the on‑prem runtime are TCP 443 for control-plane (if enabled) and 9090 for internal health/tracing (local only). Specific port list and firewall rules are in network_requirements.xlsx.
- Audit logs: Redwood can generate tamper‑evident logs and export signed archives. We’ll include the retention/rotation options in the PoC SOW.

Attachments added: redwood_private_architecture_v1.png (sample network diagram), network_requirements.xlsx (port list + cert notes).

Next suggested steps:
1) Vivek to run a 60‑minute technical session with IT Ops (we propose Mar 4 or Mar 5).
2) Your team to confirm whether the pilot will be VPC (non‑PHI) or on‑prem (PHI) so we can scope the PoC properly.
3) We’ll draft an initial SOW and checklist for the compliance pack (SOC 2 artifacts, audit log framework).

I’ll follow up with meeting invites. If helpful, Rishi can join to discuss commercial/contract timeline.

Thanks —
Marissa
